prompt:
You are a senior typographer and information designer. You lay out data tables for publication. You judge layouts by looking at the rendered result as a whole: what the table is for, how a reader scans and compares it, which columns belong together or play the same role, proportion and rhythm across columns, a clear hierarchy of headers and groups, whether rows read as units, whether words, numbers and identifiers stay intact, and how text and white space are distributed. Fewer lines or a shorter table is not automatically better, and neither is equal widths or symmetry; decide case by case and say why.

Table: Operating and Financial Metrics (language en).
Grid: 5 columns × 7 rows. Row headers: yes (first logical column identifies each row).
Per-column content facts (content px at 15px font, excluding padding):
  col 1: header "Metric" · longest unbreakable word 82px · one-line width 407px
  col 2: header "FY 2022" · longest unbreakable word 61px · one-line width 61px
  col 3: header "FY 2023" · longest unbreakable word 62px · one-line width 62px
  col 4: header "FY 2024" · longest unbreakable word 58px · one-line width 61px
  col 5: header "Q1 2025" · longest unbreakable word 63px · one-line width 63px
Each column also has 21px of padding+border, so a column given width w px shows w−21 px of text.
Available width: 360px (the dashed pink box). The column widths you choose must sum to at most 359px.
This table cannot fit without splitting words at 360px. You MAY choose a total wider than 359px (the reader then scrolls horizontally), or squeeze and accept splits — a design decision.
Fixed: content, font, 15px font size, padding, borders, colours, alignment. You control ONLY the column widths.

The image shows the table's content with every cell on one line, so you can read everything. Study it first.
1) Understand it: what is the table for, how will people read, scan and compare it, which columns play the same or similar role, which values must stay intact, which text may wrap naturally, and where existing row height could absorb wrapping.
2) Propose 3 genuinely different column-width designs for 360px (different strategies, not small variations).
Reply ONLY JSON: {"understanding":{"purpose":"","reading":"","groups":["columns that belong together and why"],"keep_intact":[""],"may_wrap":[""]},"designs":[{"name":"A","widths":[int px per column, column 1 first],"idea":"one sentence"}]}

log.raw: {"understanding":{"purpose":"A compact operating and financial KPI table for comparing six metrics across FY 2022, FY 2023, FY 2024 and Q1 2025; readers use it to scan trends over time rather than read prose.","reading":"Scan the first column down to find the metric, then read across the four period columns to compare values. The metric column is the row index; the four period columns form a matched numeric band. Long metric labels will wrap at word boundaries, and period headers can stack as FY / 2022 and Q1 / 2025, but digits and currency/percent tokens should not split.","groups":["Column 1: row-label/index column, separate from all values.","Columns 2–5: one peer group of period-value columns; equal width is appropriate because they play the same role and support across-row comparison. Q1 2025 is a shorter latest period but still belongs to this band."],"keep_intact":["Metric names' unbreakable words such as 'percentage', 'acquisition' and 'recurring' — no mid-word splits","Numeric values including $, commas, decimals and % (e.g. $1,800, 71.3%)","Year digits 2022, 2023, 2024, 2025 — headers may break only after 'FY' or 'Q1'"],"may_wrap":["Long metric labels at spaces or commas, over 2–4 lines","Period headers into two lines: FY / 2022, Q1 / 2025","Header rows and metric rows may grow taller; numeric body cells should stay on one line"]},"designs":[{"name":"A","widths":[139,55,55,55,55],"idea":"Row-label-dominant: give the metric column generous width for fast label scanning, keep year digits and metric words whole, and accept that longer currency values may split in the very tight period columns."},{"name":"B","widths":[103,64,64,64,64],"idea":"Balanced 360px compromise: keep the longest metric word whole, divide the remaining width equally across the four peer period columns, and wrap headers and labels; only the widest currency token may split."},{"name":"C","widths":[103,82,82,82,82],"idea":"No-split numeric band: keep every period column at its one-line content width so values and year headers stay intact, let metric labels wrap, and allow modest horizontal scrolling (total 431px)."}]}
